newsitem.title: INDIA: India SRF sees better financials after stake sale.
newsitem.headline: India SRF sees better financials after stake sale.

text.p: Indian tyre cord maker SRF Ltd said on Tuesday that it looked forward to a sharp fall in its debt burden and improved financial prospects after selling off a majority holding in SRF Finance Ltd.

The deal to sell 50.5 percent of shares held by SRF and its associate stakeholders to GE Capital Services, a unit of General Electric, would fetch 480 million rupees ($13.4 million) to SRF Ltd, vice-chairman Arun Bharat Ram said.
"The sale of SRF Finance is just one step in the restructuring we are doing at SRF," Bharat Ram told a news conference in New Delhi.

Besides raising money from the financial company's sale, SRF expected to get raise its paid-up equity capital by around 205 million rupees ($5.7 million) through a rights issue of shares in four to five months' time, he said.
The injection of these funds, along with some internal accruals, would help cut down SRF's debt burden to 4.5 billion rupees from around 6.0 billion rupees, he said.

SRF, which ran up a huge debt after borrowing heavily to buy a tyre cord plant from India's CEAT Ltd for 3.25 billion rupees in 1995, will now get a leaner and more efficient look focusing on core businesses, he said.
Ram said the proposed rise in the equity base from 394.4 million rupees to 600 million rupees would not adversely affect SRF's earnings per share.
"If you look at the extra earnings in terms of interest savings, that will more than make up for the rise in equity," he said.
After the financial restructuring, SRF's debt-equity ratio would come down to 1:1 from 3:1 at the beginning of 1996/97 (April-March), SRF officials said.

SRF currently holds a 40 percent market share for tyre cords in India and sees a strong potential for the business as the industry expects a global demand growth of 1.5 to 2.0 percent a year, Bharat Ram said.
"We are definitely going to be concentrating in the tyre cord business," he said, but added that he continued to see good demand and growth in fluorochemicals.

Earlier on Tuesday, GE Capital said its deal to control SRF Finance would require approval from the government's Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

This would be GE Capital's second major financial venture in India. It already has a joint venture for car finance with Maruti Suzuki, in which the Indian government and Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp are equal partners.

"The transaction allows SRF to focus on its core businesses and allows GE Capital to signficantly expand its presence in commercial vehicle and working capital financing," GE Capital said in a statement.
SRF is a leading Indian company in the field of nylon tyre cords, fabrics and fluorochemicals with some interests in engineering plastics, polyester films and eye lenses.
GE Capital Services, with assets of $200 billion, is a global, diversified financial services company.
SRF Ltd said GE Capital would pay 53.50 rupees per 10-rupee share to buy a controlling stake in SRF Finance Ltd.
At Bombay, the country's financial centre, SRF Finance's stocks closed at 52.50 rupees, down 0.50 rupees from Monday's closing price of 53.0 rupees.
SRF's shares closed unchanged at the previous day's close of 36.0 rupees.
SRF's financial details were announced after trading closed in all the stock exhanges of the country on Tuesday. ($1=35.8 rupees)
